# Purpose

This primer loads the cleaned management + lab dataset with the k7 zone
assignments from Paper 1. It describes the variables, gives a brief look at
the data by zone, and lays out the hypotheses and planned analyses for Paper 2.
 The causal ML section is a plan only.

**Overarching question:** Are the k7 soil health zones useful and accurate
benchmarks for soil health, for decision-makers and for farmers?

# Setup and data

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Paths are relative to code/; the CSV lives in data/
data_path <- file.path("..", "data", "mnglabxymet_all_v8_withclusters.csv")

raw <- read_csv(data_path, guess_max = 5000, show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(raw)
```

## Cleaning decisions

* **Zone 5 is dropped.** It has a single sample, so no within-zone analysis
  is possible. Only 6 of the 7 k7 zones contain samples (zones 1, 2, 3, 4, 6;
  zone 7 has none), leaving 5 usable zones.
* `zone` is stored as a factor.
* Yes/no management fields are converted to logical (`TRUE`/`FALSE`/`NA`).
  `"unknown"` becomes `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: clean
yn <- function(x) {
  x <- str_to_lower(str_trim(x))
  case_when(x %in% c("yes", "y") ~ TRUE,
            x %in% c("no", "n")  ~ FALSE,
            TRUE ~ NA)
}

dat <- raw |>
  filter(Cluster_k7 != 5) |>
  mutate(
    zone           = factor(Cluster_k7),
    plant_cycle    = factor(plant_cycle,
                            levels = c("annual", "perennial", "uncultivated")),
    texture_class  = factor(`texture_class.x`,
                            levels = c("Coarse", "Medium", "Fine")),
    sampling_depth = factor(sampling_depth),
    across(c(till, cover_crop, organic_amendments, compost, manure,
             livestock, irrigate),
           yn, .names = "{.col}_yn")
  )

tibble(samples   = nrow(dat),
       producers = n_distinct(dat$producer_id),
       years     = paste(range(dat$year), collapse = "–"),
       projects  = n_distinct(dat$file_names))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Repeated samples
`field_id` is a field number *within* a producer ("01", "02", …), not a
unique field ID. Producer + field is unique for nearly every sample, so almost
no fields were resampled. Repeats happen at the **producer** level: several
fields per farm, sometimes in different years. Use `producer_id` as the
grouping variable for random effects and for clustering standard errors.
:::

```{r}
#| label: field-id-check
dat |>
  mutate(field_uid = paste(producer_id, field_id, sep = "_")) |>
  summarise(samples = n(),
            unique_fields = n_distinct(field_uid),
            producers = n_distinct(producer_id),
            max_samples_per_producer = max(table(producer_id)))
```

### Indicator coverage by zone

Indicators are kept for H1 only if every zone has reasonable n. Too sparse to
use: beta-glucosidase, infiltration, penetration resistance, nematodes and
microarthropods (0–4 samples in some zones).

```{r}
#| label: coverage
p1_ind   <- c("toc_percent", "poxc_mg_kg", "ace_g_protein_kg_soil",
              "pmn_28day_mg_kg", "min_c_96hr_mg_c_kg_day")
built_ind <- c("ph", "bd_g_cm3", "cec_meq_100g")
indep_ind <- c("wsa_percent", "whc_in_ft", "total_n_percent", "ec_mmhos_cm",
               "p_olsen_mg_kg", "k_mg_kg", "s_mg_kg", "min_c_24hr_mg_c_kg_day")

dat |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(n = n(), across(all_of(c(p1_ind, built_ind, indep_ind)),
                            ~ sum(!is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(-zone) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = zone, names_prefix = "zone_")
```

# Brief EDA

## Zone profiles

```{r}
#| label: zone-profile
dat |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(
    n               = n(),
    producers       = n_distinct(producer_id),
    MAP_mm          = median(map_mm_year, na.rm = TRUE),
    MAT_C           = median(mat_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_annual      = mean(plant_cycle == "annual") * 100,
    pct_perennial   = mean(plant_cycle == "perennial") * 100,
    pct_uncult      = mean(plant_cycle == "uncultivated") * 100,
    pct_coarse      = mean(texture_class == "Coarse", na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_0_20cm      = mean(sampling_depth == "0-20 cm") * 100
  ) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))
```

## Figure 1: indicators by zone

Two Paper 1 indicators (TOC, POXC) and four new indicators not used to build
the zones. The y-axis is log scale and the dashed line is the statewide median.
Zones sharing a letter are not significantly different (pairwise Wilcoxon
rank-sum tests, Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted, α = 0.05). These are unadjusted,
exploratory comparisons. Formal tests come from the mixed models in H1.

```{r}

#| label: fig-indicators
#| fig-cap: "Selected soil health indicators by k7 zone (log scale). Dashed line = statewide median. Zones sharing a letter do not differ significantly (pairwise Wilcoxon, BH-adjusted, α = 0.05)."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
library(multcompView)

fig1_vars <- c(
  toc_percent     = "TOC (%)",
  poxc_mg_kg      = "POXC (mg/kg)",
  wsa_percent     = "Aggregate stability (%)",
  total_n_percent = "Total N (%)",
  ec_mmhos_cm     = "EC (mmhos/cm)",
  p_olsen_mg_kg   = "Olsen P (mg/kg)"
)

long1 <- dat |>
  select(zone, all_of(names(fig1_vars))) |>
  pivot_longer(-zone, names_to = "var", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value), value > 0) |>
  mutate(var = factor(fig1_vars[var], levels = fig1_vars))

meds <- long1 |> group_by(var) |> summarise(med = median(value))

# Compact letter display from BH-adjusted pairwise Wilcoxon tests
cld_letters <- function(df) {
  pw <- pairwise.wilcox.test(df$value, df$zone,
                             p.adjust.method = "BH", exact = FALSE)$p.value
  pv <- c()
  for (i in rownames(pw)) for (j in colnames(pw))
    if (!is.na(pw[i, j])) pv[paste(j, i, sep = "-")] <- pw[i, j]
  lt <- multcompLetters(pv, threshold = 0.05)$Letters
  tibble(zone = factor(names(lt), levels = levels(df$zone)), letter = lt)
}

sig_labels <- long1 |>
  group_by(var) |>
  group_modify(~ cld_letters(.x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(long1 |> group_by(var) |> summarise(ypos = max(value) * 1.6),
            by = "var")

# Overall Kruskal–Wallis test per indicator, for the text
long1 |>
  group_by(var) |>
  summarise(kruskal_p = signif(kruskal.test(value ~ zone)$p.value, 3))

ggplot(long1, aes(zone, value)) +
  geom_hline(data = meds, aes(yintercept = med),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#BCD3F2", colour = "#1F4E9C", width = 0.6,
               linewidth = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_text(data = sig_labels, aes(zone, ypos, label = letter),
            size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "k7 zone", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```


## Figure 2: management and crop composition by zone

This figure shows the confounding that the design has to handle: practices and
crop types aren't spread evenly across zones.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mgmt
#| fig-cap: "Percent of samples in each zone reporting each practice or plant cycle (NA excluded from the denominator)."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
mgmt_labels <- c(
  till_yn               = "Tillage",
  cover_crop_yn         = "Cover crop",
  organic_amendments_yn = "Organic amendment",
  compost_yn            = "Compost",
  manure_yn             = "Manure",
  livestock_yn          = "Livestock",
  irrigate_yn           = "Irrigated",
  annual                = "Annual crop",
  perennial             = "Perennial",
  uncultivated          = "Uncultivated"
)

mgmt_pct <- dat |>
  mutate(annual       = plant_cycle == "annual",
         perennial    = plant_cycle == "perennial",
         uncultivated = plant_cycle == "uncultivated") |>
  select(zone, all_of(names(mgmt_labels))) |>
  pivot_longer(-zone) |>
  group_by(zone, name) |>
  summarise(pct = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            n   = sum(!is.na(value)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(name = factor(mgmt_labels[name], levels = rev(mgmt_labels)))

ggplot(mgmt_pct, aes(zone, name, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(pct),
                colour = pct > 55), size = 3.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#EEF3FB", high = "#1F4E9C",
                      limits = c(0, 100), name = "% of samples") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20")) +
  labs(x = "k7 zone", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

### Practice sample sizes within zones

For H3, a practice is tested within a zone only with **≥15 samples with the
practice and ≥15 without**. Cells below that are flagged.

```{r}
#| label: practice-cells
min_n <- 15
dat |>
  select(zone, ends_with("_yn")) |>
  pivot_longer(-zone, names_to = "practice") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  count(zone, practice, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = value, values_from = n, values_fill = 0,
              names_prefix = "n_") |>
  mutate(practice = str_remove(practice, "_yn"),
         testable = n_TRUE >= min_n & n_FALSE >= min_n,
         cell     = paste0(n_TRUE, " / ", n_FALSE, if_else(testable, "", " ✗"))) |>
  select(practice, zone, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = zone, values_from = cell, names_prefix = "zone_")
```

Cells read as *n with practice / n without*. ✗ = below the minimum.

## Candidate reference (uncultivated) sites

Reference sites are filtered in tiers. Tier 4 here counts **date-confirmed**
sites only (≥10 years between `crop_plantdate` and sampling). Sites supported
only by free text, and sites with no date, need manual review: use
`reference_site_review.csv` and the collector contacts, or check NLCD and
historical imagery once coordinates are available.

```{r}
#| label: reference
est_year <- function(x) {
  x <- str_to_lower(str_trim(x))
  case_when(str_detect(x, "before") ~ 2000,
            str_detect(x, "^(19|20)\\d{2}$") ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)),
            TRUE ~ NA_real_)
}

unc <- dat |>
  filter(plant_cycle == "uncultivated") |>
  mutate(est      = est_year(crop_plantdate),
         yrs      = year - est,
         t1_nofallow = crop_group != "Fallow",
         t2_notill   = t1_nofallow & till_yn %in% FALSE,
         t3_noinputs = t2_notill & !(irrigate_yn %in% TRUE) &
                       !(organic_amendments_yn %in% TRUE),
         t4_dated10  = t3_noinputs & !is.na(yrs) & yrs >= 10,
         t3_undated  = t3_noinputs & is.na(yrs))

ref_tiers <- unc |>
  group_by(zone = as.character(zone)) |>
  summarise(all_uncultivated = n(),
            `1_no_fallow`    = sum(t1_nofallow),
            `2_no_till`      = sum(t2_notill),
            `3_no_irr_amend` = sum(t3_noinputs),
            `4_dated_10yr`   = sum(t4_dated10),
            undated_to_review = sum(t3_undated))

bind_rows(ref_tiers,
          summarise(ref_tiers, zone = "Total", across(where(is.numeric), sum)))
```

Reference types also differ by zone (grazed native land, CRP, forest). Report
reference type alongside any reference comparison, and consider excluding
forest as an unrealistic target for cropland.

```{r}
#| label: reference-types
unc |> filter(t3_noinputs) |> count(crop_type, zone) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = zone, values_from = n, values_fill = 0,
              names_prefix = "zone_")
```

# Hypotheses and analysis plan

## H1: Do the zones hold up with new indicators?

**Hypothesis:** Soil health indicators not used in Paper 1 differ among the
k7 zones, and the differences remain after accounting for crop and
management. This tests the strength of the k7 zones, which were built from
spatial data and validated with carbon-based indicators, using new information.

* **Indicators, in two groups.**
  * *Related to zone inputs* (pH, bulk density, CEC). Mapped SOLUS versions
    of these were clustering inputs. The lab data are independent, so these
    test whether mapped differences show up in the field.
  * *Not used to build zones* (WSA, water-holding capacity, total N, EC,
    Olsen P, K, S, Min-C 24 h). These are the stronger test: do the zones
    capture properties they were never built on?
* **Models**, per indicator:
  * Unadjusted: `indicator ~ zone + (1|year) + (1|file_names) + (1|producer_id)`
  * Adjusted: add `crop_group + plant_cycle + texture + sampling_depth +` main practices
* **Report** zone F-statistics, η² or partial R², and how much the zone
  effect shrinks after adjustment. Keep the metrics comparable to Paper 1.

## H2: How do the zones differ, by how much, and why?

**Question:** How do the zones differ in management, crop composition and soil
health? By what size and direction, and what are the primary drivers
(management, crop, soil, sampling)?

**Expectation:** Zones differ strongly in management and crop composition
(Figure 2). Once those are accounted for, the soil health differences
attributable to zone itself may be smaller.

* **Composition:** chi-square tests with Cramér's V for practices and crop
  mix by zone.
* **Size and direction:** standardized effect sizes or percent differences of
  each zone vs. the statewide mean and vs. the other zones. Show as a
  zone × indicator heatmap with direction.
* **Drivers:** variance partitioning in the mixed models (partial R² or
  commonality analysis) across zone, soil (texture), crop, management and
  sampling.

## H3: Do sustainable practices improve soil health within zones?

**Question:** Within zones, do more sustainable practices (reduced tillage,
cover crops, organic amendments, perennial cover, livestock integration)
improve soil health indicators, even after accounting for differences in soil?
How do managed fields compare with uncultivated reference sites?

* **Mixed models with a practice × zone interaction**:
  `indicator ~ practice * zone + texture + crop_group + sampling_depth + (1|year) + (1|file_names) + (1|producer_id)`.
  The interaction tests whether practice effects differ by zone. Show
  per-zone practice effects as forest plots.
* **Testable cells only.** Use the ≥15 / ≥15 rule from the practice table above.
* **Reference comparison (exploratory).** Express each field as a percentage of
  its zone's median at the confirmed reference sites, and compare across
  practice groups. Use strict (confirmed) references as the main analysis and
  broad (tier 3) references as a sensitivity check. Keep it descriptive where
  references are few (zones 2 and 6).

### Causal ML for practice effects that vary by zone (planned, not run here)

Practices are not randomly assigned. Farms that use cover crops differ in crop,
texture and location. Causal ML adjusts for those confounders and estimates how
each practice's effect varies by zone:

* **Method:** causal forests (`grf::causal_forest`) or double/debiased ML
  (`DoubleML`) for each binary practice (e.g., cover crop vs. none, no-till vs.
  tilled) and each indicator.
* **Confounders:** zone, texture/clay/sand, crop group, plant cycle, irrigation,
  MAP/MAT, sampling depth, year, project. Lab indicators are never used as
  predictors.
* **Outputs:** average effect statewide and conditional effects by zone, with
  confidence intervals, plus a formal test of whether effects differ across
  zones.
* **Checks:** propensity overlap and covariate balance in each zone. Where
  overlap fails, report the effect as not estimable instead of producing a
  number. Cluster by `producer_id` for repeated samples.
* **Role:** this complements the mixed models. Practice effects are reported as
  supported where both approaches agree in direction and size.

## Synthesis: are the zones useful benchmarks?

| Test | How | Zones are useful if… |
|---|---|---|
| Explanatory value | Compare k7 against other groupings: statewide, county, texture class, crop group | k7 explains more variance, or the same with fewer groups |
| Benchmark accuracy | Score held-out fields (grouped by producer) against zone vs. statewide percentile benchmarks | Zone benchmarks reclassify fields in agronomically sensible ways |
| Advice differs by zone | Practice × zone interaction (H3) | Practice effects differ by zone, so advice should too |
| Stability | Zone medians and rankings across sampling years | Benchmarks are stable across 2020–2024 |

## Sensitivity checks

* Drop the 0–20 cm samples.
* Drop the 2016–2019 DuPont data (`file_names == "2016-2019_dupont"`).
* Use one sample per producer (most recent).
* Rerun reference comparisons with strict vs. broad reference sets.
